The petitioner says that a circular was issued by the
 Food Safety and Standard Authority of India ("in short Fssai")

sentences.text: for  filling up of the vacancies in the posts of Management Services  and Scientific Services in FSSAI on deputation including short  term contract/contract (outsource).
The petitioner submitted his  candidature.
Admittedly, the selection process was conducted by  FSSAI.

A list of suitable candidates were short listed by the  Selection Committee and were respectively placed in a  recommendation list as serial nos.1 to 9 for being appointed Dr. Sk. 1  against the vacancy of four technical officers.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The  recommendation was approved by FSSAI by a memo dated 21 st  May, 2012 in the same order as in the recommendation list.

The  Assistant Director (E&A) of FSSAI forwarded a list of nine  candidates respectively placed in serial nos.1 to 9 to the agency  2 engaged for outsourcing technical officers being the respondent no.8.

In the memo dated 21st May, 2012 (appearing at page 42 of the writ petition) there is,
however, no mentioning of four vacancies in the posts of technical officers.

It only says that FSSAI have decided to outsource the services of the following persons in serial nos.1 to 9 through their agencies to give services in FSSAI on consolidated wages for a period upto 31 st July, 2012.
The petitioner says that he was never engaged by the agency for rendering services to FSSAI as per the memo dated 21st May, 2012 though his name appeared in serial no.2.
On the contrary, the petitioner says that the respondent no.7 who was placed as number 3 in the serial was allowed to join on 11 th June, 2012.
The petitioner says that he being placed in serial no.2 ought to have been allowed to join and render services before respondent no.7 who was no.3 in the list.

Having not done so, the outsourcing agency as well as FSSAI have acted arbitrarily and in an illegal manner, FSSAI being a government organisation, according to the petitioner could not have resorted to such untransparent arbitral procedure when they themselves had conducted an interview to select suitable candidates and had placed the petitioner in serial no.2 ahead of the respondent no.7 being placed in serial no.3.
The petitioner further submits there still lies vacancy in the post of technical officers in FSSAI as per the documents available with the petitioner, though not on record.
The petitioner, therefor, should be permitted to join as technical officer, FSSAI.
FSSAI in reply submits that they have outsourced the recruitment and had only assisted in preparing a list by conducting a selection process.
It is the agency which has given the appointment to respondent no.7.
The dispute is, therefor, inter se between the agency and the petitioner to which FSSAI has no role to play.

The writ petition is,
therefor, not maintainable.
The fact, however, remains that FSSAI had taken on itself the burden of preparing the selection list even though it had outsourced the appointment.
It was, therefor, necessary before allowing respondent no.7 placed in serial no.3 to join as technical officer in ahead of respondent no.3 as to the reasons for the same.
There is no reflection of such reason in the affidavit filed by FSSAI.

sentences.text: The subject list was prepared in the year, 2012.
Last affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioner was affirmed on 29 th July, 2016 i.e. more than five years prior to this date.
Things have changed during the interregnum period of five years.
Many factors are required to be considered before a final decision can be arrived at in the writ petition.
It is required to be seen whether there is any age bar in respect of a person to be engaged and permitted to work as technical officer in FSSAI.
It is also necessary to know whether there exists any vacancy in the post of technical officer in FSSAI at the present if, so, what is the exact number of vacancy.
It is also necessary to know whether anyone else apart from respondent no.7 has been allowed to work as technical officer in FSSAI from out of the list prepared and forwarded on 21st May, 2012.
The affidavit of FSSAI is silent as to the basis and on what yardstick the petitioner was placed in serial no.2 and respondent no.7 in serial no.3.
The general perception will be that a person placed in serial no.2 is found to be more suitable than those placed below him, FSSAI is the best person to provide these information to the Court.
FSSAI is, therefor, directed to file a supplementary affidavit giving the detailed facts and figures with regard to the matter observed hereinabove to enable the Court to take a conscious decision.
The supplementary affidavit shall be filed by 7 th January, 2022 with a copy to the petitioner and other respondents.

It is made clear that in the event no supplementary affidavit is filed by FSSAI as directed, no further extension will be granted and an adverse presumption will be drawn as against FSSAI for not furnishing the facts and figures required by this Court for effective adjudication of the matter.
Let this matter appear on 13th January, 2022.
(Arindam Mukherjee, J.)
